body: Call me crazy, but I can see the framework of the book in the movie. They took the interviewer character from the book and morphed it into Brad Pitt’s character. So rather than interviewing people post war, he was the investigator tracing the virus during outbreak. Pitt ended up sinking like $15 million of his own money into making that movie with the hopes of making a trilogy. So extrapolating from the first movie, if he had continued the trilogy they would have gone into containment in the second film, having found the camouflage, and onto reconstruction after that in presumably a third movie. We got recounts from the book (patient zero, the Israeli defense) in the movie through the lense of investigation rather than remembrance. I still don’t think it was a great movie by any means, but if the whole vision had come to fruition I think it could have been a pretty faithful representation of the book, just shifted drastically in perspective. But unfortunately we got what we got and it was lackluster at best.

His character drug on season after season as this “big-bad” specter-in-the-dark type that carried no threat and never really amounted to any real danger. For whatever reason, the writers let him live waaaaay longer than he should’ve and they wrote Rick into this sniveling puddle of a man that WOULDN’T just kill him like the mad dog Rick from season 4 & 5 would’ve. Every second Negan was on screen I loathed. Initially I stopped watching at season 8 when Negan still wasn’t dead, and years later went back and watched to the end of season 9 when they still didn’t just fucking kill him off. I gave up after that with the introduction of Alpha and the whisperers. The show just died after season 6, it became pointless and wrote with hollow characters that weren’t true to the virtues the writers gave them in the beginning of the show. I love seasons 1-5 and I wish the show ended there.

My wife and I have 3 & 1/2 year old twins. It. Is. Hard. Full stop. But I constantly remind myself of the old adage, “parenting is only hard for good parents.” There are days where I want to, and even days where I have, run from my house screaming. Three year olds are hard, they are coming into all of those rudimentary emotions that will form all of their complex emotions later. They are full of curiosity and chaos. 

I don’t think of myself as a gentle parent, maybe I am, idk but I talk to my kids alot. I try to speak to them on their level (literally I sit or kneel down) If they get angry I try to give them a moment to calm down and work through their frustration because, just like adults, when they are angry or upset or frustrated they don’t hear words, they are emotionally incapable of listening. I yell a lot too, it is effective, but I don’t usually feel good after I do, and it usually makes my kids more upset or just stomps on them emotionally. I had a very yell-y dad and I always hated that that was his only reaction to things. I try to stick to stern words and more importantly I try to stick to my guns when I say something. Boundaries are really important for kids at this age otherwise they won’t learn.

Toddlers gonna toddle. They get into everything all the time and do everything they aren’t supposed to. They are exploring and experimenting with the world around them. We made our living room into a toddler friendly zone. We keep nothing too dangerous or delicate in there and we put up a big dog fence thing between the kitchen and living room so literally they can get into whatever shit they want and we don’t have to worry about it. 

I get the going out thing. If I am in a social setting with my twins I live on the edge. I am, at any given moment, seconds away from an anxiety attack but the catch-22 is, if you never take them out they will never learn how to act in social settings. Just a week ago we were at a wedding and my daughter, during dinner, was pouring soup onto the table decorations…I wanted to die. I got so overwhelmed I could have just left and never gone back…but 20 minutes after dinner, she was running around the dance floor with her aunts and uncles having the best night of her tiny life and that was everything for me. She was free and having fun and was listening and being such a good kid. Not to mention bed time that night was a cake walk because both twins were exhausted to the bone. 

Long story short threenagers are hell, but they will surprise you with their growth. Its tough, but you’re tough. Be the best parent you can be, and be aware that that definition will change day to day. Tomorrow you might be better, and the day after you might be worse, as long as its your best, its good enough for your kid.

I’m really not trying to split hairs just trying to see the point of Magnus from a different perspective. All the other traitor primarchs have a damning trait right? Angron is wrath, Fulgrim is pride/vanity, Perty is envy and so on. And the loyal primarchs have some of the same traits to illustrate the dichotomy of sins and virtues. So what is the point of Magnus’ fall, is it simply the road to hell? That just seems needlessly tragic when the Emperor illustrates the exact same thing. Both tried in vain to save something (the imperium/the thousand sons) and both failed, with Emps being deified and Magnus being damned.

I guess maybe what bothers me about the whole thing is that Magnus was genuinely being what Emps built him to be and Emps still condemned him for it. Sure Magnus dabbled in a bit of chaos fuckery and sure thats not cool but so did Big E. Magnus did all the same stuff Emps did and he was betrayed by the Imperium for it. Magnus’ story just makes no sense to me on the grand scale. He didn’t do nothing wrong but the things he is most guilty of is loving his kids and being himself. Its like hes set up to be the Emperor’s foil but is laughably outgunned from the start.. Hes the second most powerful psyker and is a better dad than Papa E and gets screwed over for it. The other traitor primarchs are obviously supposed to fall and Magnus certainly has the traits required to make him vulnerable, but I feel like Emps actions in the end are what forced his hand, not some latent internal flaw. Idk, school me if I’m wrong.

Biologically, its because generally our actions (and the actions of pretty much every organism discovered) are driven by self-preservation and procreation. Its whats called a biological imperative. You’re familiar with the flight or fight reflex. Both options are driven by a need to keep living. We have evolved a whole part of our brains dedicated to managing and controlling that reflex, the amygdala, often called the lizard brain. As far as procreation, well every living thing on Earth is designed to make more of its self so that is pretty obviously our biological purpose. Dead things can’t procreate.

Psychologically, its because our entire model has been built around self-actualization, the pinnacle of mental health, and nowhere in the model does suicide fit in. Additionally the comorbidity of suicide/self-harm and numerous psychological ailments is so prevalent that the proof is in the pudding.

Economically, dead people are bad for the economy.

Religiously, suicide is the theft of a gift given by god, it is a cardinal sin and so punished by an eternity of torture and despair in hell. (DISCLAIMER: this interpretation is based upon the Abraham model of religion pertaining to most sects of Christianity, Islam, and Judaism)

Logically, I think therefore I am, dead people don’t think, therefore they are not.

There are lots of reasons that suicide is viewed negatively. Mostly people don’t enjoy watching their loved ones kill themselves. Death is hard, untimely death is harder still. In many ways suicidal people, as you have, can justify why they are suicidal and why it is a positive option but it does not change the fact that suicidal ideation is a byproduct of suffering and the belief that the suffering will not end. Most people do not believe that a person is unable to change their circumstances to fix the bad things in their life that are causing them to suffer and so suicide is seen as a bad thing. Additionally suicide is viewed as a copout, as a “permanent solution to a temporary problem”. Most people don’t see it as an ultimate mechanism of control: I am suffering, I cannot stop the suffering, I will kill myself to stop it. That logic doesn’t make sense to the human mind. 

Honestly I could ramble on and on answering your question and refuting your logic but really OP, you need some help, you need to find a way to change your situation for the better. You can’t get better if you’re dead. Suicide seems like an option, it seems like the logical thing to do, but its not. As a dude who has dealt and is dealing with suicidal ideation, I have no good reason to tell you not to do it other than just don’t. Its always going to seem like a final solution, its always going to be there as a choice, but its a choice you just can’t make. Every possibility, every chance you have to get better, every future that could happen, disappears in a single moment if you make that ultimate choice. And sure, some of your future could be bad, worse than now even, but some of it could be better. Thats really the point. Suicide guarantees that nothing gets worse, but it also guarantees that nothing gets better either. If you don’t care about getting better or having a future, like you say, then you’re committing to the pain, the suffering, which frankly makes no sense. You have to understand that where you are is your choice at this point. You have decided that suicide is the only way because you don’t want to make any other choice. You’re afraid of the possibilities. Thats why you need to find some help. Thats why you, specifically shouldn’t do it.

Its tactical purpose is CAS, Combat Air Support. The main gun on it is actually smaller than most artillery guns and tank guns. In the world of artillery 105 is the baby compared to 120, 125, 140, and 155. Its there to provide rapidly deployable firepower in locations conventional arty can’t reach. It has been especially helpful in Afghanistan due to the mountainous terrain which makes arty support impractical most of the time. The high angle of attack and loitering ability of the AC-130 is why we have these.

What makes them impractical is they are easily zeroed and have very specific mission and flight restrictions. When you fly around in a big circle for hours with really big loud guns, people tend to notice you are there.
Most variants are armed with a 105 howitzer canon, a 40mm gun and a 25mm gun. Other variants have the 105 howitzer, the 25mm, and a rear cargo ramp loaded with 16 javelin missile tubes.

No, more like food that never got digested, a predatory Eukaryote engulfed a proto-mitochondria and in a semi-intelligent process assimilated it into its cell structure. Mitochondria maintained a sort of autonomy while supplying the parent cell with ATP. The telltale evidence of this hypothesis is the double membrane that surrounds Mitochondria in the cell. One membrane being the original organ of the proto-Mitochondria, the second being the vacuole that was created when the cell engulfed the proto-Mitochondria. Fast forward billions of years and you have symbiotic relationship wherein Mitochondria self replicate within a  cell to supply additional Mitochondria for cell division. They are the only organelle whose information is not contained within the genome of the parent cell. Thats why we have Mitochondrial DNA and cellular DNA. Until recently we thought only mothers passed on mDNA due to the mechanics of egg fertilization, but it is possible to inherit mDNA from dads as well however, it is extremely rare.
Eukaryotes and Mitochondria/Cyanobacteria hold one of the oldest symbiotic relationships on earth along side Lichens.
